ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Julius Caesar

code.originalText: Ten-week review: seizure control, lipids on atorvastatin, blood pressure, and driving and safety

text.paragraph: Ten-week review: seizure control, lipids, blood pressure, and driving. [S]

Julius Caesar returns ten weeks after starting levetiracetam, atorvastatin, and aspirin, and six weeks after amlodipine was added. He has had no seizure, spell, or confused awakening, and has missed no doses. He has had slight ankle swelling in the evenings, which he does not mind. His home readings are 118 to 128 over 72 to 80. He has no muscle aches, bleeding, or bruising, and his mood is good. He asks when he can drive again and whether he can stop any of the medicines in time. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Regular rhythm; blood pressure 124/76 mmHg; trace ankle edema

Recurrent transient episodes of collapse: six days ago a witnessed collapse with stiffening and jerking of both arms for about a minute, a bitten tongue, and about twenty minutes of confusion, after a rising strange feeling and dizziness; two briefer spells of staring and unresponsiveness in the past eighteen months; cause not yet known (seizure, convulsive syncope, or transient ischemic attack)
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented accounts of falling attacks and fainting fits; it resolves when the cause is found.
Hypertension, stage 2: 152/94 and 148/92 mmHg today; told of high blood pressure about three years ago and never treated
S — Synthetic vascular risk factor; no blood pressure from his lifetime is known.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 158 mg/dL, triglycerides 170 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL
S — Synthetic vascular risk factor; no lipid value from his lifetime is known.

Focal epilepsy with a structural vascular cause: focal impaired-awareness seizures with automatisms, one evolving to a bilateral tonic-clonic seizure, arising from a chronic left temporal cortical infarct, with left temporal sharp waves on EEG
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to the documented falling attacks; the ILAE 2017 seizure types and a structural cause are chosen for teaching and make no claim about what he had.
Chronic left posterior temporal cortical infarct, not recognized before the seizures, with moderate small-vessel white matter disease and a non-stenotic left carotid plaque; no residual deficit
S — Synthetic modern finding anchored to the retrospective cerebrovascular hypothesis; it makes no claim about his real brain.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection with low-grade fever and poor sleep, three weeks after starting levetiracetam; rapid COVID-19 and influenza tests negative; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness, chosen to teach cold-remedy choices with hypertension, aspirin, and an antiseizure medicine, and sleep loss as a seizure trigger; it echoes no documented illness.

list.item:
Focal epilepsy on levetiracetam (G40.209). Seizure-free for ten weeks on 500 mg twice daily; mood good (PHQ-9 3, item 9 scored 0). With a structural cause the risk of recurrence stays high, so treatment is long term; any later trial off medicine would be a decision with his neurologist after at least two seizure-free years. [S]
Continue levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily.
Neurology review at six months.
Driving: not before the seizure-free period that state law requires (six months in this state) and his neurologist's clearance.

Chronic left temporal cortical infarct (I69.398). LDL 68 mg/dL, below 70, and ALT 34 U/L on atorvastatin 80 mg. Blood pressure at target. No new symptoms. [S]
Continue aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 80 mg.
Lipid panel every 6 to 12 months.

Hypertension (I10). 124/76 mmHg in the office and at target at home on lisinopril and amlodipine; trace edema is tolerable. [S]
Continue both medicines.
Potassium and creatinine once a year.

Hyperlipidemia (E78.5). LDL fell from 158 to 68 mg/dL. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 80 mg.
